Why don't birds on power lines get fried? That wire is carrying thousands of volts.
Here's the secret. Electricity only flows when it has somewhere to go.
It moves from high voltage to lower voltage, like water flowing downhill.
A bird sits with both feet on the same wire. Both feet are at the same voltage. No downhill. So no current flows through the bird.
But if a bird touches two wires at once, or a wire and the pole... zap. Now there's a path.
That's why big birds like eagles are in danger. Their wings are wide enough to touch both.
And it's why you should never go near a fallen power line. You're standing on the ground. You become the path.
